added_after_first_run: Run 38256846461 (the first timed run) existed when three variants were added: m05_stride2.span_il2 and m08_matmul.span_il2 (the span rewrite plus #pragma clang loop interleave_count(2), because the span rewrites vectorized with interleave 1 under FAST and stayed 1.1x to 1.4x slower) and m06_gather.clamp (clamp every index into range, trap after the loop). They are judged by the same rules below; no rule or threshold was changed.
headline_rule: A rewrite is called better (it recovers the speed with hardening on) only when it keeps safety AND recovers on every CPU model drawn. Otherwise its ratios are reported without that word.
note: derived by scripts/build_site_data.py from results/mitigate-run-*/mitigate-*/results.json, mitigate/criteria.json and mitigate/src/
recovered_rule: A variant RECOVERS the speed on a job when, at both L1 and L2, the upper end of the 95% interval of vs_original_aligned is at most 1 + (that job's A/A half-width for the kernel and size) / 100. It recovers on a CPU model when it recovers on every usable job of that model.
rules_written: The rules for reading the mitigation experiment (mitigate/run.py). Written and committed BEFORE the first timed run of .github/workflows/mitigate.yml. Compiler Explorer (clang 18.1.0, x86-64) was used to check that each rewrite compiles and to read its vectorization remark; no timing of any rewrite existed when this file was written.
